## 1. Purpose

This module closes the simulated-data workflow by comparing all seven genomic
prediction methods on exactly the same outer-assessment individuals defined in
M02:

- `GBLUP_A`, `GBLUP_AD`, and `GBLUP_ADE`;
- `ANN_0`, `ANN_L1`, `ANN_L2`, and `ANN_L1_L2`.

Predictive performance is evaluated using the known **true simulated genetic value** as the primary target. The **observed phenotype** is a complementary target because it includes residual variation.

The six C1-C6 settings represent **simulated genetic scenarios**, not
six unrelated measured traits. They differ in QTL number and nominal
heritability, and model performance is compared separately in each.

The comparison follows three principles:

- all seven methods use the same 25 outer-assessment tasks per scenario;
- each task evaluates the same 200 held-out individuals for every method;
- each of the twelve metrics is plotted separately for C1-C6, without a
  performance mean that combines all six scenarios.

Because repeated outer-assessment sets overlap, the figures are descriptive
and do not treat folds as statistically independent replicates.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/simulated/comparison/figures",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)
```

## 2. Packages, saved results, and compared methods

### 2.1 Packages

The module uses `knitr` for result tables and `ggplot2` with `ggthemes`
for figures. Performance results were computed in M03 and M04 and are
read from saved files; no prediction model is refitted here.

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
```

### 2.2 Saved prediction results

GBLUP and ANN task-level metrics and individual held-out predictions are
stored in separate RDS files. Read the four inputs directly, as in M03/M04.

```{r saved-model-results}
# Read saved task metrics from the two model-fitting modules.
gr <- readRDS("output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds")
ar <- readRDS("output/simulated/ann/final/simulated_ann_results.rds")

# Read individual held-out predictions for matched assessment checks.
gp <- readRDS("output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.rds")
ap <- readRDS("output/simulated/ann/final/simulated_ann_predictions.rds")
```


The next table counts the records read from the four archived objects.

```{r saved-inputs-summary}
input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "GBLUP task-by-model results",
    "GBLUP held-out predictions",
    "ANN task-by-model results",
    "ANN held-out predictions"
  ),
  Rows = c(nrow(gr), nrow(gp), nrow(ar), nrow(ap)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Saved results entering the seven-model comparison",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The inputs contain 450 GBLUP task-by-model results, 600 ANN task-by-model
results, 90,000 GBLUP held-out predictions, and 120,000 ANN held-out
predictions. The comparison comprises the prediction results from all seven models.

### 2.3 Compared genomic prediction methods

The comparison includes three GBLUP structures from M03 (additive,
additive-dominance, and additive-dominance-epistatic) and the four
regularization variants from M04. These identifiers select the existing
result records; they do not define or fit new models.

```{r compared-models}
# Fix the scientific model order and display labels.
expected_gblup_models <- c(
  "GBLUP_A",
  "GBLUP_AD",
  "GBLUP_ADE"
)

expected_ann_models <- c(
  "ANN_0",
  "ANN_L1",
  "ANN_L2",
  "ANN_L1_L2"
)

model_order <- c(
  expected_gblup_models,
  expected_ann_models
)

model_labels <- c(
  "GBLUP-A",
  "GBLUP-AD",
  "GBLUP-ADE",
  "ANN-0",
  "ANN-L1",
  "ANN-L2",
  "ANN-L1+L2"
)
```
### 2.4 Matched tasks and assessment individuals

The next steps establish equivalent assessment records for the seven methods.
Because the GBLUP `TaskID` is model-specific, cross-method matching uses
the model-independent outer-split keys (`Scenario`, `Repetition`, `Fold`, and
`SplitID`); prediction records additionally use the individual identifier `ID`.

```{r matched-keys}
split_keys <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID"
)

prediction_keys <- c(
  split_keys,
  "ID"
)
```

The following counts establish model-by-task coverage and the number of predictions within each held-out task.

```{r matched-task-structure}
model_structure_rows <- vector(
  "list",
  length(model_order)
)

for (model_index in seq_along(model_order)) {
  model <- model_order[model_index]

  if (model %in% expected_gblup_models) {
    result_data <- gr[gr$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
    prediction_data <- gp[gp$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    result_data <- ar[ar$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
    prediction_data <- ap[ap$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  result_task_key <- do.call(
    paste,
    c(result_data[split_keys], sep = "__")
  )
  prediction_task_key <- do.call(
    paste,
    c(prediction_data[split_keys], sep = "__")
  )
  predictions_per_task <- table(prediction_task_key)

  model_structure_rows[[model_index]] <- data.frame(
    Model = model,
    Tasks = length(unique(result_task_key)),
    Predictions = nrow(prediction_data),
    Min_predictions_per_task = min(predictions_per_task),
    Max_predictions_per_task = max(predictions_per_task),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

model_structure <- do.call(rbind, model_structure_rows)
rownames(model_structure) <- NULL
```


Each of the seven models should contribute 150 tasks and 200 assessment predictions per task.

```{r matched-task-table}
knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  '<div style="max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto;">',
  as.character(
    model_structure |>
      knitr::kable(
        format = "html",
        caption = "Observed task and assessment structure for the seven methods",
        row.names = FALSE,
        table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="white-space:nowrap;"'
      )
  ),
  "</div>"
))
```

Cross-model matching uses scenario, repetition, fold, split ID and individual ID. The model-specific TaskID is deliberately not a matching key.

```{r matched-targets}
all_predictions <- rbind(
  gp[, c(prediction_keys, "Model", "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value")],
  ap[, c(prediction_keys, "Model", "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value")]
)

reference_model <- model_order[1]
reference_targets <- all_predictions[
  all_predictions$Model == reference_model,
  c(prediction_keys, "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value"),
  drop = FALSE
]

target_match_rows <- vector("list", length(model_order) - 1L)

for (model_index in seq_along(model_order[-1])) {
  model <- model_order[-1][model_index]
  candidate_targets <- all_predictions[
    all_predictions$Model == model,
    c(prediction_keys, "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  matched_targets <- merge(
    reference_targets,
    candidate_targets,
    by = prediction_keys,
    suffixes = c("_Reference", "_Candidate"),
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )

  target_match_rows[[model_index]] <- data.frame(
    Reference = reference_model,
    Model = model,
    Reference_predictions = nrow(reference_targets),
    Model_predictions = nrow(candidate_targets),
    Matched_predictions = nrow(matched_targets),
    Phenotype_difference = max(abs(
      matched_targets$Observed_Phenotype_Reference -
        matched_targets$Observed_Phenotype_Candidate
    )),
    TrueG_difference = max(abs(
      matched_targets$True_Genetic_Value_Reference -
        matched_targets$True_Genetic_Value_Candidate
    )),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

target_match <- do.call(rbind, target_match_rows)
```


The following table reports the reference and candidate record counts,
individual-level match coverage, and maximum paired differences. Full
coverage requires 30,000 matched records per model, with zero differences
for both evaluation targets.

```{r matched-target-table}
knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  '<div style="max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto;">',
  as.character(
    target_match |>
      knitr::kable(
        format = "html",
        digits = 12,
        caption = paste("Maximum paired target difference relative to", reference_model),
        row.names = FALSE,
        table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="white-space:nowrap;"'
      )
  ),
  "</div>"
))
```

Every model contributes 150 tasks with 200 held-out predictions per task.
All six comparisons recovered `r paste(unique(target_match$Matched_predictions), collapse = ", ")`
matched observations, the same number as the available records per model.
The maximum paired differences in phenotype and true genetic value are zero,
confirming equal evaluation targets for these matched individuals.

## 3. Evaluation metrics

The seven models are assessed using the same held-out performance measures. For individual $i$, let $p_i$ be the prediction, $t_i$ the evaluation target, and $n=200$ the size of each assessment set. True genetic value and observed phenotype are evaluated separately.

- **Pearson correlation** measures linear association between prediction and
  target; larger values are better.
- **Spearman correlation** measures monotonic rank association between prediction
  and target; larger values are better.
- **RMSE** and **MAE** measure prediction error on the original target scale;
  smaller values are better.
- **Bias** is `mean(prediction - target)` and is retained as a complementary
  calibration measure; values nearer zero are preferable.
- **Slope** is the prediction coefficient in `lm(target ~ prediction)` and is
  retained as a complementary calibration measure; values nearer one are
  preferable.
- No \(R^2\) metric is used.

The prediction errors and bias on the original target scale are
\[
\mathrm{RMSE}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(p_i-t_i)^2},\qquad
\mathrm{MAE}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|p_i-t_i|,
\]
\[
\mathrm{Bias}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(p_i-t_i).
\]
The calibration slope is the coefficient of the prediction in
$t_i=\alpha+\beta p_i+\varepsilon_i$. Pearson measures linear association,
and Spearman measures rank association. Each metric is calculated within
each outer-assessment task before the task-level values are averaged.

For all twelve measures, the figures display **25 task-level observations
within each scenario and model**. White diamonds show means *within*
individual C1-C6 scenarios, not across scenarios. Bias is assessed relative
to zero, and slope relative to one.

```{r metric-definitions}
metrics <- c(
  "Genetic_Pearson",
  "Genetic_Spearman",
  "Genetic_RMSE",
  "Genetic_MAE",
  "Genetic_Bias",
  "Genetic_Slope",
  "Phenotype_Pearson",
  "Phenotype_Spearman",
  "Phenotype_RMSE",
  "Phenotype_MAE",
  "Phenotype_Bias",
  "Phenotype_Slope"
)
```

## 4. Comparison against true genetic value by scenario

The known true genetic value is the **primary prediction target**.
All seven methods are compared for each of the six metrics and for each
C1-C6 scenario. C1-C6 differ jointly in QTL number and nominal heritability,
so scenario differences cannot be attributed to either factor in isolation.

Within each panel, boxplots summarize 25 held-out task values, points show
each task, and white diamonds mark within-scenario means. The shared metric
scale enables comparison across the six panels. Because repeated splits
overlap, the figures do not imply independent replication or significance.

```{r comparison-task-results}
# Reuse the task-level metrics from M03 and M04 without refitting models.
analysis_cols <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID",
  "Model",
  metrics
)

all_results <- rbind(
  gr[, analysis_cols],
  ar[, analysis_cols]
)

# Keep scientific model IDs in the results; display friendly labels in figures.
plot_results <- all_results
plot_results$Scenario <- factor(
  plot_results$Scenario,
  levels = paste0("C", 1:6)
)
plot_results$Model <- factor(
  plot_results$Model,
  levels = model_order,
  labels = model_labels
)
```

The scenario-specific averages below are retained only for optional export;
the figures preserve the 25 values rather than replacing them with a mean.

```{r scenario-performance}
# Average tasks within each scenario/model only, never across C1-C6.
# The figures use all_results itself and retain the full task distributions.
scenario_summary <- aggregate(
  all_results[, metrics],
  by = list(
    Scenario = all_results$Scenario,
    Model = all_results$Model
  ),
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

scenario_summary <- scenario_summary[
  order(
    scenario_summary$Scenario,
    match(scenario_summary$Model, model_order)
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

### 4.1 Pearson correlation

Larger values indicate stronger linear association.

```{r genetic-correlation-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, fig.cap="True genetic value: pearson correlation across C1-C6, with 25 outer-task observations per model and scenario. White diamonds denote within-scenario means."}
# Each facet is one simulation scenario, preserving all outer assessments.
p_genetic_pearson <- ggplot(
  plot_results,
  aes(x = Model, y = Genetic_Pearson, fill = Model)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.58,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.70
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.10,
      height = 0,
      seed = 20260821L + 501L
    ),
    alpha = 0.28,
    size = 1
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 2.7,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario, ncol = 2) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gdocs() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "True genetic value: Pearson correlation",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)
  )

print(p_genetic_pearson)
```

```{r save-model-correlation-tiff, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
# Export the same figure in TIFF format for publication.
ggsave(
  "output/simulated/comparison/figures/model_genetic_correlation_comparison.tiff",
  plot = p_genetic_pearson,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 12,
  height = 10,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

## 5. Comparison against observed phenotype by scenario

Observed phenotypes include residual variation alongside genetic effects.
The same seven methods and held-out outer partitions are compared for the
same six metrics, separately in each scenario. Interpret these results as a
complement to, not a replacement for, recovery of true genetic value.

### 5.1 Pearson correlation

Larger values indicate stronger linear association.

```{r phenotype-pearson-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, fig.cap="Observed phenotype: pearson correlation across C1-C6, with 25 outer-task observations per model and scenario. White diamonds denote within-scenario means."}
# Each facet is one simulation scenario, preserving all outer assessments.
p_phenotype_pearson <- ggplot(
  plot_results,
  aes(x = Model, y = Phenotype_Pearson, fill = Model)
) +

### 5.7 Regularization effects among ANN models

ANN-0, ANN-L1, ANN-L2, and ANN-L1+L2 share the architecture and learning rate
selected with ANN-0 within each outer task, as described in M04. Their
differences in the figures are therefore conditional on that shared
selection rule. Interpret the four regularization variants *within each
scenario and metric*; do not assign an overall winner from a mean that
combines the six scenarios.

## 6. Scientific conclusion

The seven genomic prediction methods were evaluated on matched outer tasks
in six distinct simulated genetic settings. The twelve reported metrics
are shown separately by C1-C6 and by evaluation target, without averaging
performance across the six scenarios.

Pearson and Spearman quantify linear and rank association; RMSE and MAE
quantify prediction error; bias and slope assess calibration relative to
zero and one. Descriptive differences do not establish statistical
significance or a universal ranking across simulation settings.
The scenario-specific means can optionally be exported for inspection,
but no global model performance summary is generated.

```{r save-comparison-summaries, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Optional: export scenario-specific means for external inspection.
dir.create(
  "output/simulated/comparison",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  scenario_summary,
  "output/simulated/comparison/simulated_model_scenario_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
